title: Free to choose (5:1)
hook: every person is given free will; this is a great principle
tomorrow: if God knows what i'll choose, am i still choosing?

segments.voice: Yesterday: clear the path. Gossip and mockery hold back return, but they don't close it. Which raises a bigger question about the person doing the clearing.

It's how I'm wired. My family's just like this. That's my sign, so of course I'm stubborn. Reasons like these are easy to reach for when a choice gets hard. Some of them hold a little truth. But is the choice to change really yours? Maimonides opens chapter five by answering that before anything else, and he doesn't hedge.
screen: `IT'S HOW I'M WIRED.` → `IS THE CHOICE REALLY YOURS?` → `HE DOESN'T HEDGE.`

segments.voice: Freedom, he writes, is given to every person. If someone wants to turn toward the good and be righteous, the power is in their hand. If they want to turn the other way, that's in their hand too. He reads a strange verse from the garden this way: "Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil." Humans, he says, know good and evil from within themselves, and nobody holds their hand back. Then he names the idea he's arguing against. Don't believe, he says, that God decrees at a person's birth whether they'll be righteous or wicked. Every person can become righteous like Moses or wicked like Jeroboam, wise or foolish, merciful or cruel. And he calls this a great principle, a pillar of the whole Torah, because commands only make sense if you can choose to keep them. His verse is from Deuteronomy: "See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil." Set before thee. Not decided for you. That's why return, all those chapters of it, is possible at all. Wiring and family and habits are real pressures. But in Maimonides' picture, they push. They don't decide. You're free to choose.
screen: `THE POWER IS IN YOUR HAND.` · `NO DECREE AT BIRTH.` · `MOSES OR JEROBOAM.` · `SET BEFORE THEE.` · then, large: `FREE TO CHOOSE.`

segments.voice: Take a pen. Write one small choice waiting for you today, then write the words I choose, and finish the sentence on purpose rather than by default. Read it back once, slowly, and sit with the feel of a decision that's actually yours.
Free to choose: Maimonides' great principle. Freedom is given to every person to turn toward good or away from it, and nothing is decreed at birth.
Your line: free to choose. Wiring and habits push hard, but they don't decide. See you tomorrow.

notes: Hilkhot Teshuvah 5:1–3 paraphrased; Maimonides' reading of Genesis 3:22 (the human species unique in knowing good and evil of itself) is summarized. Confirm.

'Don't believe … that God decrees at a person's birth': Maimonides attributes this view to 'fools among the nations and most of the unlearned of Israel'; the voice omits the attribution to avoid a slight against anyone. Confirm.
